changes: First RINGMOD SC release: an insert whose gain follows another track's audio. DUCK pulls the gain down with the key's peak over the last one to two HOLD windows (13-26 ms by default), so it holds through a kick's zero crossings and steps down as it decays; ATK softens the fall and REL the recovery. RING multiplies the audio by the key, a ring modulator whose carrier is any of T1-T8. Main page: KEY (OFF, T1-T8), DPTH and KLPF over ATK, HOLD and REL; MODE (DUCK, RING) on SETUP. DPTH 0 or KEY OFF passes the audio bit for bit.

In RING the three DUCK knobs shape the carrier and are named SLEW, S&H and RECT there: S&H takes a new key every 16 samples a step and holds it between (stepped modulation); RECT blends the key toward its rectified copy, at 127 doubling the carrier's frequency and keeping it non-negative (an AM-like modulation), ramped so it does not click; SLEW above 0 drives the gain with the key's level, smoothed from 0.7 ms to 1.3 s, a tremolo that follows the key; turning it to or from 0 (or a lock or an LFO crossing 0) crossfades over 16 samples instead of clicking, and turning S&H down cuts the current hold short. At 0 each is a plain copy, so RING with all three at 0 is the plain ring modulator; the knobs keep their values when MODE changes, so turn S&H and RECT to 0 after switching a fresh instance to RING. MODE reads like a stock select (MODE over DUCK or RING).

It reads the Modwerk base's key bus over USB (loader ABI 9, requires the key bus): no tap of its own and nothing written outside its own state, so it runs beside Sidechain Compressor. While it is installed the base's tap copies every track on both cores, and its price (41 executed instructions a sample a core, counted from the source, charged at 7/4) counts toward RINGMOD SC. It is USB-only: a card image has no key bus, so the configurator does not build card firmware with it (one built anyway keeps its depth at 0 and passes the audio untouched).

Key latency is the bus's: exact from a track dispatched earlier on the same core, 16 samples from one dispatched later, 32 across the cores (measured on an MKII for Sidechain Compressor and on the key bus re-check, not yet as heard through this module). 351 DSP words, 22 words of state, no buffer; 63 instructions a sample in either mode by static count; 80.56 executed instructions a sample at worst measured (DUCK with a trig split; RING 79.19).

Hardware: this package ran on the author's MKII over USB on 22 October 2026 (a RAM-booted development twin of the beta base): DUCK, plain RING, RECT, SLEW through 0 and S&H turned down by ear, two instances on both cores and slots, Part and project reload, every install and removal order beside Sidechain Compressor, and the base's self-test passed.

Limits: parameter locks and LFOs, scenes, eight instances a core and a power cycle have not run on a unit, and the key latency is carried from the 21 October key bus re-check; a slow SLEW stops a little short of the key's level (up to about 1.4% of full scale at 127, as the review measured on the build before) and a very quiet key never raises it; an LFO on S&H makes S&H 0 a hold of 1-15 samples; DUCK buzzes at its very shortest ATK, HOLD and REL (audio-rate amplitude modulation, as expected); on a base from before the module select step fix (now on main's beta base) KEY may move a track a detent on the first visit to the main page; installing Sidechain Compressor while it is live re-zeroes the bus once, about a block of silent key. Scenes and a power cycle are untested.
